report.summary: Chunk 9 of 11 of canary.py: contains `grade` function completing ProbeResult construction, `_run_lane` function for sequential per-lane probing, and `run_canary` function orchestrating the canary run with live check and threading.
risks: _run_lane | medium | Uses broad except BaseException which may mask unexpected errors | Confirm if catching BaseException is intentional to prevent any crash from taking down the canary

run_canary | medium | Threads are daemon and abandoned at wall clock; potential resource leaks if threads hold resources | Verify that resources (e.g., network connections) are cleaned up or that abandonment is acceptable

run_canary | low | `max_parallel` is clamped to at least 1, but Semaphore with max_parallel=1 still allows one thread at a time; naming may be misleading | Confirm intended behavior: max_parallel=1 means one thread at a time?

run_canary | low | `live_egress_lanes` is called before run_id and nonce creation, but the docstring claims 'before the run id, before a nonce, before a thread, before one byte is dispatched' – check if this ordering is guaranteed | Verify that no side effects occur before this check

handoff.purpose: Contains grade function completing ProbeResult, _run_lane for sequential probe execution per lane, and run_canary orchestrating the canary run with live check and threading.

symbols.name: grade
symbols.note: Constructs ProbeResult from lane, probe, nonce, reply, and latency. Uses _TRANSPORT_MAP (not visible in chunk) to map reply status. Trims reply to REPLY_TRIM.

symbols.name: _run_lane
symbols.note: Runs probes in a lane sequentially within a single thread. Uses gate semaphore, deadline, and nonce_factory. Catches BaseException to prevent lane from crashing the canary.

symbols.name: run_canary
symbols.note: Main entry point for running canary probes. Checks live flag and raises LiveCanaryRefused if non-live and live egress lanes detected. Creates threads with daemon flag, uses Semaphore for parallelism, and returns a CanaryRun.

claims.text: Sequential within a lane on purpose: four concurrent calls to the same vendor is a load test, not a health check
claims.why: The function iterates over probes sequentially in a for loop without spawning additional threads.

claims.text: it would make the latency numbers -- the thing the trailing median compares -- meaningless
claims.why: The chunk does not show the trailing median calculation; this claim refers to logic outside the chunk.

claims.text: It is also what keeps a hung vendor to ONE occupied slot rather than four.
claims.why: The function uses a semaphore (gate) to limit concurrency, and sequential execution per lane ensures only one probe per lane is active at a time.

claims.text: Threads are DAEMONS and are ABANDONED at the wall clock rather than joined
claims.why: The chunk shows thread creation with daemon=True but does not show the join/abandon logic; the wall clock timeout handling is not fully visible.

claims.text: a thread cannot be killed, so a hung vendor must degrade the report instead of blocking it.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the mechanism that handles hung threads; only thread creation is visible.

claims.text: Every abandoned (lane, probe) is still reported -- as ``timeout``/``wall_clock``
claims.why: The chunk does not show how abandoned probes are collected or reported; only the planning loop is visible.

claims.text: ``live`` is the SPEND OPT-IN and defaults to False.
claims.why: The function signature shows `live: bool = False`.

claims.text: Any lane that still carries a shipped vendor transport (:func:`live_egress_lanes`) raises :class:`LiveCanaryRefused` here -- before the run id, before a nonce, before a thread, before one byte is dispatched
claims.why: The code calls `live_egress_lanes(lanes)` and raises `LiveCanaryRefused` before creating run_id, nonce, or threads.

claims.text: Fake lanes are unaffected, so the offline harness never has to ask for permission it does not need.
claims.why: The chunk does not define what constitutes a fake lane; relies on `live_egress_lanes` which is imported.

claims.text: Materialised ONCE, before anything inspects it: the gate below iterates the roster, and a one-shot iterator would arrive here full, be drained by the gate, and reach the scheduling loop empty -- a canary of no lanes, reported as if it had run.
claims.why: The code converts `lanes` to a tuple immediately, ensuring it is materialized once.

observations.what: `grade` function uses `_TRANSPORT_MAP` which is not defined in this chunk; it is imported or defined elsewhere in the file.
`_run_lane` catches `BaseException`, which is very broad; it may catch `SystemExit` or `KeyboardInterrupt`.
`run_canary` creates threads with `daemon=True` and does not join them; the wall clock timeout is not fully shown.
`max_parallel` is clamped to `max(1, int(max_parallel))`; if `max_parallel` is 0, it becomes 1.
